description: Figure 2 illustrates the training loss as a function of the number of steps for various model types, categorized by their size, under a fixed dataset size of 20 million. The x-axis represents the training steps, plotted on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to approximately 2000 steps, with tick labels appearing at regular intervals of 500 steps. The y-axis represents the training loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to approximately 1.5, with tick labels appearing at regular intervals of 0.25. The plot contains multiple lines, each corresponding to a different model type and size. The lines are distinguished by color and marker shape, with solid lines generally representing larger models and dashed lines representing smaller models. All lines exhibit a downward trend, indicating a decrease in training loss over time, with the rate of decrease varying between model types. For instance, the line for the smallest ChemBERTa model starts at a loss value of approximately 1.2 and decreases to about 0.6 by step 2000. In contrast, the line for the largest ChemBERTa model begins at a loss value of approximately 1.0 and decreases more rapidly to about 0.35 by step 2000. The lines for BART and RoBERTa-based models start at similar loss values and decrease at a comparable rate across all sizes shown.
